entries.title: two-failure reachability oracle
entries.statement: **Theorem 1.1 (two-failure reachability oracle).** Every such \(G,r\) admits a deterministic combinatorial index constructible in \(O((n+m)L^3)\) time and \(O(n+m)\) working words. The completed index occupies \(O(n)\) words. Given \(F\) and \(t\) after construction, it decides reachability in \(O(L^3)\) time using only the index and the query.
claim_facets: every later failure set and target

entries.title: listed target sets
entries.statement: **Corollary 1.2 (listed target sets).** Let \(q\) queries specify failure sets \(F_i\) with \(|F_i|\le 2\) and target lists \(T_i\). Put \(M=\sum_i|T_i|\) and \(S=n+m+q+M\). The Boolean vector whose entry \(i\) says whether at least one target in \(T_i\) survives can be computed in \(O(SL^3)\) total time and \(O(S)\) working words, including construction. A single list presented later takes \(O((1+|T_i|)L^3)\) query time.

entries.title: sibling quotients
entries.statement: **Lemma 2.1 (sibling quotients).** Each \(H_d\) is a rooted DAG in which deleting any nonroot vertex loses only that vertex. Paths through the blocks project to paths in \(H_d\), and a quotient path lifts through any chosen sequence of its labelled arcs. Across all \(d\) there are at most \(2n\) vertex copies and one quotient arc per retained original arc.

entries.title: last-exit test
entries.statement:
**Lemma 2.2 (last-exit test).** Every target outside \(D(d)\), and \(d\) itself, survives. A target in \(D(u)\) survives precisely when \(a\) does not dominate it, with the symmetric rule for \(D(v)\). For a target in a third block \(D(y)\), it survives if \(y\notin J(B)\). If \(y\in J(B)\), it survives precisely when
\[
 \sigma^B_u(y)\notin D(a)\quad\text{or}\quad \sigma^B_v(y)\notin D(b).
\]

entries.title: forest of proper losses
entries.statement: **Lemma 3.1 (forest of proper losses).** There is a rooted forest with one node for each pair \(B\) with \(J(B)\ne\varnothing\), and a label \(c(y)\) for each vertex of \(H\). Adjoin an artificial root \(0\) above all forest roots, allowing \(c(y)=0\). For every real pair \(B\), \(y\in J(B)\) precisely when \(B\) is an ancestor of \(c(y)\), with ancestry inclusive. A real child \(P\) of a real parent \(B\) satisfies \(P\subseteq Z(B)\) and \(J(P)\subseteq J(B)\). Every vertex in \(P\setminus B\) follows both endpoints of \(B\) in topological order. There are at most \(|V(H)|\) real forest nodes.

entries.title: constructing the forest
entries.statement: **Lemma 3.2 (constructing the forest).** On a flat quotient with \(n_H\) vertices and \(m_H\) labelled arcs, the labels and pair forest can be built in \(O((n_H+m_H)L^3)\) time and \(O(n_H+m_H)\) working words. After construction, \(O(n_H)\) words suffice for pair lookup in \(O(L)\) time and, for a known pair node, proper-loss membership in \(O(1)\) time.

entries.title: exit transfer
entries.statement:
**Theorem 4.1 (exit transfer).** Let \(P\) be a real child of a real pair \(B\) in the forest of \(H_d\). For each \(s\in B\) and \(y\in J(P)\),
\[
 X^B_s(y)
   = \bigcup_{p\in P\setminus B} X^B_s(p)
      \ \cup\
      \begin{cases}
        X^P_s(y), & s\in P,\\
        \varnothing, & s\notin P .
      \end{cases}
\]
The union over fresh endpoints is independent of \(y\).

entries.title: compressed exit summaries
entries.statement: **Lemma 5.1 (compressed exit summaries).** Within \(H_d\), one can compute a base vector of two original-tree LCAs for each vertex with a real label and two constant-size maps for each real pair node. These records recover both values \(\sigma^B_s(y)\), \(s\in B\), for any \(y\in J(B)\) in \(O(L^3)\) time. Building the records takes \(O((n_H+m_H)L^3)\) time and \(O(n_H+m_H)\) working words given the original-tree operations below. The retained records use \(O(n_H)\) words.

entries.title: a guarded output of residual multiplicity two
entries.statement: **Corollary 6.1 (a guarded output of residual multiplicity two).** For one supplied healthy-zero guarded output with \(\mu\le2\), the existence of an admissible detecting set is decidable in \(O(G_{\rm dec}\log^3(G_{\rm dec}+2))\) time and \(O(G_{\rm dec})\) working words. A positive answer identifies an admissible detecting set.

entries.title: higher sensitivity
entries.statement: **Question 6.2 (higher sensitivity).** For arbitrary \(\mu\ge3\), can a deterministic combinatorial algorithm decide whether any listed target survives in any query on a DAG in \(\widetilde O(2^\mu S_\mu)\) total time, where \(S_\mu=n+m+q+\sum_i (|F_i|+|T_i|)\) and \(|F_i|\le\mu\)?

open_boundaries: Question 6.2 asks about deterministic total cost for arbitrary sensitivity at least three.
